brief.data: Codebook v3.2 with 46 variables in 7 groups: identifiers, article metadata (outlet, date, section, word count, byline type), framing (primary frame and headline frame from 9 options), sources (up to 12 sources, each with name, role from 14 categories, and whether directly quoted), policy mentions (17 checkboxes), tone (5-point scale), and coder notes. The reliability sample is 10% of articles, double-coded, with Krippendorff's alpha so far 0.81 on framing and 0.74 on sources.

prompt:
I need the front end for Codebook Desk. A research data-entry tool a university journalism school's local news research lab uses to have trained coders record structured content-analysis codes for thousands of newspaper articles.

Who's using it: Halima Yusuf, a second-year master's student and one of six paid coders on the lab's project studying how 40 US local newspapers covered housing affordability from 2019 to 2025. She was trained on the codebook three weeks ago and codes in two-hour stints between classes.

What they're doing right now: She's on article 318 of her assigned batch of 600, a 1,400-word Fresno Bee piece on a rent-control ballot measure. She has filled in most of the 46 variables. The system just flagged two problems. She coded 'primary frame' as 'Economic' but chose 'Human interest' for the headline frame, which the codebook says requires a note when they differ. She also marked 'Tenant voices quoted: none' while entering two named sources with the role 'renter'. She has to check the article text, fix the source entries or the tenant code, add the required justification note, and submit. Then the next article loads. Article 322 is in the inter-coder reliability sample, so it will be compared with another coder's work.

What's in the system at this point: Codebook v3.2 with 46 variables in 7 groups: identifiers, article metadata (outlet, date, section, word count, byline type), framing (primary frame and headline frame from 9 options), sources (up to 12 sources, each with name, role from 14 categories, and whether directly quoted), policy mentions (17 checkboxes), tone (5-point scale), and coder notes. Validation rules include required fields, allowed ranges, and cross-field consistency checks (21 rules). Halima's batch: 600 articles, 317 submitted, 4 returned by the supervisor for correction. Her average time is 11 minutes per article. Project total: 9,412 articles, 5,870 coded. The reliability sample is 10% of articles, double-coded, with Krippendorff's alpha so far 0.81 on framing and 0.74 on sources.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
